title: They 'left him like a dog:' SIU called after Niagara cops fatally shoot man on New Year's Eve
subtitle: Family and the SIU identified the victim as Fred "Troy" Penner
article: The family of a 56-year-old man killed by police is "infuriated" and allege officers on scene didn't do enough to save him after shooting him to death.
The Special Investigations Unit says it was called after the fatal shooting in St. Catharines on New Year's Eve.
Family and the SIU identified the victim as Fred "Troy" Penner.
Melissa Lane, whose partner is Fred's nephew, told CBC she saw a video on social media which appears to show the moments after police shot Penner.
"They just left him like a dog."

The fatal shooting happened, police say, after officers were called to the area of Rykert Street and Edith Street in St. Catharines at about 4:30 p.m. on Tuesday following the report of a man armed with a knife.
Police say that when officers arrived, an altercation ensued and the man was shot.
Penner was taken to hospital for treatment of life-threatening injuries and the SIU said Thursday morning he died in hospital on Wednesday at 12:27 p.m.

It is unclear how long the video, shot by someone who says he was a neighbour, was recorded after the shooting occurred. It shows the victim on the ground at the foot of a driveway and begins with officers gathered around the victim.

CBC has viewed the clip that appears to show an officer reach down to Penner at 15 seconds and again at 30 seconds, and they wait some 60 seconds later before getting what appears to be equipment to check Penner's vital signs. In the video, no officers are seen with their weapons drawn.

"I watched a video of officers standing around a man on the ground without trying to help him. I was watching without sound feeling horrible for this man and his family only to find out after that the man in the ground was my own cousin ... my family is 'the family,' " Cheryl Penner, Fred's cousin, told CBC.

Neil Taylor, 19, says he lives on Rykert Street, a few doors down from Penner. The street is a quiet one, so when he thought he heard "fire crackers" he checked outside, only to find his neighbour on the ground with officers standing over him.
Taylor said police didn't immediately tend to Penner, who didn't appear to have a weapon.
"They were trying to use vehicles to block the scene," he told CBC. "It felt really weird, How they were trying to hide it that much ... nobody has answers."
Lane said police didn't act quick enough.
"He wasn't even really dead yet... they just assumed he was dead and left him lying there and they all look like they're just standing around," she said.
"Nobody covered him up for a while. They were more worried about themselves ... he didn't deserve that."

The SIU says it is prohibited from providing further information at this time and did not confirm whether it is aware of the video or whether it is investigating allegations of a lagged response from police.
Niagara Regional Police also could not comment.
Lane said Penner lived with mental illness and lived in a home on Rykert Street in St. Catharines.
They knew he wasn't doing well when he didn't show up to her mother in-law's home for Christmas dinner.
"He normally shows up every Christmas. We always looked forward to seeing Uncle Fred for Christmas," Lane said. "He was a little bit of a character."
While she says Penner was unemployed, he lived a successful life and worked a number of odd jobs.
And when he was well, he was "very kind."
"He always let everyone get their dinner before him. He was humble," Lane said.
A community vigil is set to take place tomorrow at 7:15 PM at St. Anthony Catholic Elementary School on Rykert Street in St. Catharines.
